title: Empirical Test of the Universality of Superposition in Aligned Models

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: If alignment changes superposition geometry unpredictably, this directly impacts the reliability of mechanistic interpretability for aligned models. The finding would inform whether mech interp tools need to be recalibrated post-alignment.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Sparse autoencoder training on Pythia models is becoming more accessible with open-source SAE libraries. However, comparing base vs. RLHF models requires loading large models, and interpreting SAE features for safety relevance requires domain knowledge. Medium compute is borderline for Pythia models.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Core comparison (base vs. aligned model SAE features) is well-defined. But training SAEs, comparing feature dictionaries, and identifying safety-relevant features adds up. Could be scoped to one model pair and a small set of predefined safety concepts.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Novelty not assessed due to partial Wave 3 completion.
